channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Cooperation With UN Secretary-General
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek. Guterres congratulated Uzbekistan on its 35th independence anniversary. They discussed strengthening cooperation with the UN and its institutions, and Guterres welcomed Uzbekistan's achievements in Sustainable Development Goals.

item.title: Uzbek President and Chinese President Discuss Strengthening Comprehensive Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek. Mirziyoyev thanked Xi for congratulations on Uzbekistan's independence anniversary and contributions to bilateral relations. They discussed elevating ties, trade, investment, and cultural exchanges, noting bilateral trade neared $18 billion last year.

item.title: Lesson Recalls Value of Free Thought on Day of Remembrance for Repression Victims
item.description: August 31 marks the Day of Remembrance for Victims of Repression, a reminder of past tragedies and the importance of historical experience. The Jadid movement, advocating national development and modern statehood, was suppressed by the totalitarian Soviet system for threatening national consciousness and free thought.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Cooperation with UN, President Meets UN Chief in Bishkek
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand cooperation with the United Nations. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres in Bishkek to discuss pressing issues. The meeting took place during the President's visit to the Kyrgyz capital.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China agree to boost trade to $30 billion and invest in energy
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in Bishkek, agreeing to increase bilateral trade to $30 billion and explore joint investment projects worth $60 billion. They discussed cooperation in energy, including peaceful nuclear power, and the BYD electric vehicle production. A key focus was the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project.

item.title: Russia and China may make visa-free travel regime permanent
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated Russia is ready to work with China to make the existing visa-free travel regime between the two countries permanent. Putin expressed readiness to continue cooperation on this matter during a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Bishkek.

item.title: Bishkek Summit to Test SCO's Economic Ambitions, Media Reports
item.description: The Bishkek Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation will focus on advancing the SCO Development Bank, Development Fund, and Investment Fund. Al Jazeera notes that while political agreement on the Development Bank was reached previously, specific operational parameters remain undefined, testing the transition from political statements to practical agreements.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China leaders discuss trade, aim to increase volume to $30 billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and China's President Xi Jinping met in Kyrgyzstan to discuss bilateral issues. They proposed increasing trade volume between the two countries from the current $18 billion to $30 billion.

item.title: Russia and China may establish permanent visa-free regime, Putin states
item.description: Russia is ready to establish a permanent visa-free regime with China, stated Russian President Vladimir Putin during a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Bishkek. Putin expressed readiness to continue working on this issue with the Chinese side.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Iran leaders discuss energy cooperation and new transport routes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Bishkek to discuss bilateral relations. The leaders focused on trade, energy cooperation, and expanding transport and logistics ties, as well as cultural exchange and international issues.

item.title: Russian President Putin arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit to attend the 6th World Nomad Games and the SCO Heads of State Council meeting. He will also hold bilateral talks with several leaders and Russia will assume the SCO presidency in 2027-2028.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes New System for Preserving Memory of Victims of Repression
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed developing a new system to preserve the memory of victims of political repression and those who died for the country. He noted the expansion of work to perpetuate their memory in recent years and called for similar efforts for victims of the 1980s "cotton case."

item.title: Turkish President Erdogan arrives in Kyrgyzstan for working visit
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his wife, Emine Erdogan, arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit. They were welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. Erdogan is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with several heads of state in Bishkek.

item.title: Kyrgyz and Mongolian Presidents Discuss Joint Projects and Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh to discuss strengthening bilateral ties. They emphasized leveraging historical and cultural connections for concrete trade, economic, and transport projects benefiting citizens and businesses.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes expanding cooperation with India in pharmaceuticals and IT
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss trade, investment, and healthcare cooperation. Japarov highlighted education, medicine, pharmaceuticals, and IT as key areas. Both leaders agreed to elevate bilateral ties to a new level.

item.title: Five years of "NarcoSTOP": How a prevention project became a platform for systemic change
item.description: The "NarcoSTOP" project in Almaty, active since 2022, has evolved beyond combating drug graffiti. It now focuses on adolescent prevention, aiding addicts and families, providing legal consultations, and analyzing data to understand risk factors for drug use. Specialists aim to refine prevention strategies based on collected data.

item.title: Ukraine may strike Russia using Starlink, seeking permission for drone use
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has reportedly asked Elon Musk for permission to use Starlink-equipped drones to strike Russian targets up to 200 kilometers inside Russian territory. The request aims to counter Russian ballistic missile launch devices, according to a Financial Times report.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit to attend the SCO Heads of State Council meeting, a high-level "SCO plus" meeting, and the opening ceremony of the Nomad Games. He was gifted a snow leopard toy, a national symbol of Kyrgyzstan. Kyrgyzstan will chair the SCO in 2026.

item.title: Tajikistan's National Bank to pilot e-wallet taxation from September 1
item.description: The National Bank of Tajikistan announced a three-month pilot program for taxing individual entrepreneurs' transactions via e-wallets, starting September 1. The system aims to tax business operations through e-wallets. Previously, a 3% tax rate was proposed for commercial transactions, down from 6%. Details on transaction limits remain unclear.

item.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine cause casualties and power outages in six regions
item.description: Russian strikes on Ukraine have disrupted power supply in six regions: Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Sumy, and Mykolaiv. National energy company Ukrenergo reported that emergency repairs are underway where security permits. Two people died and two were injured in Kherson following drone attacks. Two more residents died in central Kherson, and several others were injured in drone attacks.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon discusses cooperation and regional security with US representatives
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with US Special Envoy for Central and South Asia Sergio Gor and Senator Steve Daines in Bishkek. They discussed cooperation, regional security, and trade-economic interaction, including investment in energy, industry, and mining. The C5+1 platform was highlighted as important for regional dialogue.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Ends Summer With Growth Amid High Inflation and Business Contraction
item.description: Kazakhstan's economy grew 4.1% in January-July, despite a 8.9% oil production decline. Inflation reached 10.2% year-on-year in July. The National Bank lowered its base rate twice, but credit remains expensive. Small and medium-sized businesses decreased by 8% compared to last year.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Bishkek to participate in the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and a meeting in the 'SCO Plus' format. He will also attend the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Arrives in Bishkek Accompanied by His Wife
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Bishkek with his wife to attend the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting and a 'SCO Plus' format meeting. He was welcomed by Kyrgyz officials at Manas International Airport. The president will hold bilateral meetings and attend the World Nomad Games opening ceremony.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan replaces ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has appointed Nazarali Oripov as the new ambassador to Tajikistan. Oripov replaces Erlan Abdildaev, who had served as ambassador since April 2022 and was dismissed in July. Abdildaev has since been appointed ambassador to Hungary.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Seeks Easing of US Visa Bond Requirements
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan met with U.S. Special Envoy Sergio Gor to discuss simplifying visa requirements for Kyrgyz citizens traveling to the United States. They specifically addressed reviewing the visa bond requirement and other restrictions. Gor expressed readiness to strengthen Kyrgyzstan-USA relations and discussed political dialogue, trade, and investment cooperation.

item.title: SCO Summit and State Visits to Bishkek: Developments Today
item.description: Bishkek is hosting events related to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit and official visits by heads of state on August 31 and September 1, expecting 21 presidents and prime ministers. Unprecedented security measures are in place. The SCO marks its 25th anniversary, with the summit on September 1. Meetings between Armenian and Azerbaijani leaders, and the arrival of the Pakistani Prime Minister are noted.

item.title: Armenian PM Pashinyan Reports Meeting with Azerbaijani President Aliyev in Bishkek
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced on social media that he met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Bishkek. Pashinyan shared footage of the negotiations. Further details about the meeting and the topics discussed were not immediately available. Both leaders are in Kyrgyzstan to attend the SCO Plus high-level meeting and the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.

item.title: Afghanistan does not pose a threat to neighboring countries, says Taliban representative
item.description: A representative of Afghanistan's interim government, Zabihullah Mujahid, responded to statements about supplying weapons to the Tajikistan-Afghanistan border. Mujahid stated that Afghanistan does not pose a threat to its neighbors. This statement comes after reports of an agreement to strengthen the border.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sees Togo as a promising partner in Africa
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with Togo's Prime Minister, Fara Essossimna Gnassingbé, who is attending the SCO Plus meeting and World Nomad Games. Japarov stated Kyrgyzstan views Togo as a key partner on the African continent and thanked Togo for supporting Kyrgyzstan's UN Security Council bid.

item.title: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrives in Kyrgyzstan for working visit
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan arrived in Kyrgyzstan on August 31 for a working visit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport and received a stuffed snow leopard toy, the national symbol and mascot for the World Nomad Games.

item.title: Kazakhstan's healthcare and social services volume exceeds one trillion tenge in Q2 2026
item.description: In the second quarter of 2026, healthcare and social service organizations in Kazakhstan provided services worth over 1.05 trillion tenge. The Medical Services Fund (MSF) covered nearly half of this amount. Hospital organizations accounted for the largest share of services, followed by other healthcare activities and general medical practice.

item.title: Pakistan Culture Days to be held in Tajikistan in 2027
item.description: Pakistan Culture Days will take place in Tajikistan in 2027 as part of cultural cooperation. The event aims to introduce Tajikistan's residents to Pakistani culture, art, and literature. Meetings with cultural representatives and exhibitions are planned.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev travels to Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has departed for Bishkek on a working visit. He will attend the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and a "SCO Plus" format meeting on August 31.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Calls US Economic War Against Tehran a "Failed Policy"
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described US President Donald Trump's threat to initiate an economic war against Tehran as a continuation of Washington's "failed policies." This statement criticizes the US approach to economic pressure on Iran.

item.title: Yerlan Karin Appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree appointing Yerlan Karin as the country's Vice President. The appointment follows parliamentary approval, with 141 out of 145 deputies supporting Karin's nomination. This new role was established under the new constitution.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Arrives in Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at the airport by Kyrgyzstan's acting Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev and other officials. The presidential press service reported on the arrival.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes New Funding Rules for Private Schools
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Education has proposed new rules for funding private schools that operate under the state order. The ministry suggests establishing a fixed funding amount, independent of the annual increase in the monthly calculated indicator (MRP), to ensure educational accessibility and stability.

item.title: Infrastructure Development Fund Established as Treasury Account in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Infrastructure Development Fund will operate as a special account within the state treasury, rather than a separate organization. This fund will finance major national infrastructure projects, with payments disbursed in stages based on work completion, as reported by Orda.kz.

item.title: China proposes 'Water Silk Road' via Irtysh River for Arctic access
item.description: China, Kazakhstan, and Russia are discussing a project to transform the Irtysh River into a cargo corridor with Arctic access, dubbed the 'Water Silk Road'. This route, originating in China and flowing through Kazakhstan and Russia to the Arctic Ocean, could offer China an alternative to vulnerable maritime routes. Infrastructure development, including dams and dredging, would be necessary.
